pr_snapshot.body:
VP8's x64 limited 16x16 pointer SAD rebuilds slice windows and reduces every row even when the bound rules out early exits. Route its public caller through a fixed-window Go SIMD kernel, use independent even/odd PSADBW accumulators for full bounds, and preserve exact first-exceeding-row results and runtime-disabled raw-pointer behavior.

On ARM, express batch-quantizer EOB masking with AndNot so Go generates two BIC instructions instead of two MVN/AND pairs. Quantized coefficients, EOB values and alias/store order stay exact.

Native Apple M4 Max, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six balanced confirmation rounds:
- Quantizer batches of 8/16/25 blocks improve 1.038/1.080/1.086x over main, all six pairs faster, zero allocations. These new gains are below 1.5x; previously merged >=1.5x kernels remain retained independently.
- Whole VP8 is mixed: 300 frames -3.053% vs main (5/6 faster), 60 frames +0.556% (2/6 faster). It still takes 8.342%/11.004% more time than assembly. All 23 non-timing fields match. No general whole-codec gain or closure of the ARM gap is claimed.
Native x64 CI, EPYC 7763, Go 1.27.2, PGO off, six paired rounds against merged main `33c53431` and old assembly `691cd051`:
- All 20 public pointer-SAD fixtures improve in every pair. Full/wide bounds improve 2.147–2.160x, early bounds 1.665–1.666x, middle 1.029–1.193x, and near bounds 1.009–1.018x over main. Twelve fixtures exceed 1.5x in every pair. Full/wide cases take 11.89–16.13% less time than assembly; early/middle/near cases still take 20.87–88.02% more time.
- The older slice-caller `BenchmarkSAD16x16LimitEarly` regresses 3.783% versus main in all six pairs and takes 100.195% more time than assembly. Preserve this exception rather than treating pointer gains as a gain for every caller.
- Whole VP8 is +0.326% versus main (2/6 pairs faster); VP9 320 is -0.878% (6/6), VP9 720 +0.159% (2/6). On this CPU they take 14.875%/38.980%/46.586% less time than assembly respectively. These results do not close previously observed ARM or other x64 CPU gaps. Short CPU profiles do not sample the limited-pointer symbol, so they do not establish material whole-codec contribution from this kernel.
- All 114 kernel cases have six samples per variant, zero B/op and zero allocs/op. All 22 semantic fields match in three public and two profile datasets. Preserve VP9 720 baseline allocation outliers: assembly round 4 and main round 2 have 1.266667 allocations/input versus the usual 1.25; all current rounds remain 1.25. Other public/profile allocation samples match.
- Retain all 42 median-regressing controls. All-six-slower controls besides the old early-SAD are SSE16x16 +0.880%, SixTap 4x4/2,4 +4.850%, SixTap 8x8/3,5 +0.342%, and SplitSubpel 8x4 +2.384%.

Optimized libvpx v1.16.0 comparison runs separately on EPYC 9V45 with runtime CPU dispatch and SSE2/AVX2/assembly objects enabled. Fixed-speed VP8 takes 2.480x libvpx time (9.991 versus 4.028 ms/input), with matching measured PSNR, SSIM, payload size and encoded/dropped counts; this is measured-output agreement, not a bitstream identity assertion. Adaptive VP8 is +72.827% and VP9 +165.041%/+178.845%, with different quality/output work. Every quality-pass output statistic matches its corresponding timed output; all reference timers use vpxenc statistics. Do not compare absolute timings across these jobs.

Exact-head hosted, native and optimized-C checks pass. Required native validation contains 73 top-level tests plus six new panic child probes (79 targeted checks; 101 PASS lines including older subtests), no failures/skips, and confirms main/current SIMD dispatch. Raw artifacts: [native](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39061516999/artifacts/12112490725), [optimized C](https://github.com/thesyncim/govpx/actions/runs/39061516999/artifacts/12112065326).

Validation: full native tests, quantizer race/checkptr2, purego/nosimd SAD+Quant semantic checks, and exact-source AMDv1 ordinary/checkptr2/AVX-off oracles pass. AMD invalid-window child probes, disabled backwards/zero-stride windows and all 20 public benchmark fixtures pass; zero fixture allocations. The public AMD wrapper remains inlined. PGO profile/fingerprint and source/build-selection gates refreshed.

Preserve PR28's full native x64 and optimized-libvpx audit under `benchmarks/baselines/go127-simd-amd64/2026-10-17-arm-sad-control`: its EPYC9V74 VP8 control still trails assembly by 12.241%; separate EPYC7763 fixed-speed VP8 uses 2.491x optimized libvpx time with matching measured quality/output statistics. New raw component/whole measurements, exact sources, codegen and correctness evidence are under the dated `sad-pointer` and `quant-eob` baseline directories. README unchanged.
